selection: not a sibling outlier > careful pitch measurable > tone model places it clearly in its written tone > medoid (smallest median XLS-R distance to same-speaker toneless siblings)
caveats: XLS-R features are largely insensitive to tone: sibling matching and distances group syllables by toneless base, and tone is judged only by pitch (the speaker's tone model).
A syllable changes with its place in a word and its neighbours, so siblings are evidence about how the speaker says it, not exact templates.
A type recorded once has no same-tone alternative; one whose toneless base occurs in no other word has no sibling evidence at all.
Tone clarity comes from an unvalidated model (careful-take acoustic support for the written tone).
